questions.question: Explain the difference between trade discount and cash (settlement) discount, including which one is recorded and the test that separates them.
questions.expected_answer: Trade discount reduces the price at the moment of sale and is never recorded separately — the sale is simply recorded at the reduced price. Cash/settlement discount rewards prompt payment of an existing account and IS recorded: discount allowed (expense) when granted to debtors, discount received (income) when received from creditors. Test: price reduced before recording = trade; existing debt settled for less afterwards = cash discount.

questions.question: Contrast financial and managerial accounting using the four pairs from the lesson, with one example question each branch would answer.
questions.expected_answer: Financial: backward-looking, rule-bound (GAAP), standardised statements, for outsiders — e.g. 'what profit did the shop make last year?' Managerial: forward-looking, no external rules, any useful format, for insiders — e.g. 'should the shop open a second branch next year?' The pairs: past/future, outsiders/insiders, rules/freedom, report card/game plan.

questions.question: Describe what happens in the records at the moment of a sale under the perpetual inventory system, and why this makes the year-end stocktake a CHECK rather than a discovery.
questions.expected_answer: Two things are recorded simultaneously: the sale at selling price, and cost of sales at cost price moving out of Trading Stock. The Trading Stock account therefore always shows what should be on hand, so the physical count is compared against it — any gap (e.g. R48 000 expected vs R46 500 counted) is a named, investigable loss instead of being silently absorbed as sales, which is what happens under the periodic system.
